parameters.name: OnDateSelect
parameters.description: Invoked when the user selects a date/time range (click-drag on the grid).

parameters.name: OnEventChange
parameters.description: Invoked when an event's time window changes via drag or resize, alongside EventsChanged.

parameters.name: NowIndicator
parameters.description: Show the current-time indicator line in time-grid views. Default: true.

parameters.name: SlotMinTime
parameters.description: Earliest visible time slot in time-grid views (e.g. 07:00). Default: 00:00 — the full day.

parameters.name: SlotMaxTime
parameters.description: Latest visible time slot in time-grid views (e.g. 22:00). Default: 24:00 — the full day.

parameters.name: SlotDuration
parameters.description: Duration of each time slot row in time-grid views. Default: one hour. Values that do not divide an hour are rounded up to one that does.

parameters.name: VisibleDays
parameters.description: How many days MultiDay shows, and the step size when paging through it. Clamped to 1..14. Leaving this unset hides the view's toolbar button entirely — an N-day view with no N is not a view. First-party engine only; see MultiDay.

parameters.name: TimelineUnit
parameters.description: Column granularity for Timeline — a day, a week, or a calendar month per column. Default: days.

parameters.name: TimelineColumns
parameters.description: How many columns Timeline spans. Default 14. Kept separate from VisibleDays because the two count different things: a timeline column is one TimelineUnit — a day, a week or a month — while VisibleDays always counts days.

parameters.name: TimeZone
parameters.description: IANA time zone the grid is READ in, e.g. "Europe/Berlin". Unset renders the values exactly as given. Only events carrying a real instant move — see SchedulerTimeZoneProjection for why DateTimeKind decides, and why a caller passing naive wall-clock values (the overwhelming majority) sees no change at all. Edits are converted back before they reach OnEventChange/EventsChanged, so what you get out is in the frame you put in. An id this host has no data for degrades to "no projection" rather than failing the render. First-party engine only.

parameters.name: Resources
parameters.description: Optional list of resources (people, rooms, equipment). When provided, events are color-coded by their ResourceId and a legend is rendered above the calendar. Note: this colour-codes events by resource. Resource is what lays out one lane per resource.

parameters.name: Calendars
parameters.description: The calendars events can belong to. Supplying any renders a row of visibility chips, and an event whose CalendarId names a HIDDEN calendar is left out of every view. An event with a null CalendarId belongs to no calendar and is therefore never hidden — hiding "Team" must not silently swallow everything unfiled.

parameters.name: PaneMode
parameters.description: Whether visible calendars share ONE view (Overlay, the default and the behaviour before calendars existed) or each get their own pane side by side. Two-way bindable, so a caller can drive the mode from its own chrome.

parameters.name: PaneModeChanged
parameters.description: Raised when the user switches modes with the toolbar's own control.

parameters.name: BuiltInEventDialog
parameters.description: Opt into the built-in create/edit dialog. OFF by default, and deliberately so: most callers already have their own appointment form, wired through OnDateSelect and OnEventClick, and a dialog that appeared on its own would fight it.

parameters.name: EventClassNames
parameters.description: Optional callback that returns extra CSS class names for an event chip. The classes are appended to the event chip's own. Use for conditional styling without touching Color.

parameters.name: EventColor
parameters.description: Optional callback that returns a CSS color string for an event. Applied to the event chip's background and text colour. Supersedes Color when both are set; resource color applies as a fallback when neither is set.

@code {
    private SchedulerDropResult ValidateDrop(SchedulerEvent ev, SchedulerScheduleDropContext ctx)
    {
        if (ctx.ProposedStart.Day == 15) return SchedulerDropResult.Reject;
        if (ctx.ProposedStart.Day == 22)
        {
            var snapped = ctx.ProposedStart.AddDays(1);
            return SchedulerDropResult.AcceptWith(new SchedulerDropAdjustment(
                Start: snapped, End: snapped + (ctx.ProposedEnd - ctx.ProposedStart)));
        }
        return SchedulerDropResult.Accept;
    }
}

parameters.description: First day of the week for grid layout. Default Monday.

parameters.name: ShowWeekNumbers
parameters.description: Renders an extra leading column with each row's ISO-8601 week number (ReUI parity — its event calendar exposes a "week numbers" display toggle). Default false: when off, the grid keeps its exact previous 7-column markup, so this cannot shift any existing layout. The number is always the ISO-8601 week (ISOWeek), computed from each row's own THURSDAY. Thursday is ISO's defining day — the week a Thursday falls in IS its ISO week — and every 7-day row contains exactly one Thursday no matter which FirstDayOfWeek the grid starts on. That makes the label independent of the grid's start day, which a naive "first cell of the row" reading is not: in a Sunday-start grid the leading Sunday belongs to the PREVIOUS ISO week, so reading the row's first cell would label most rows one week too low.

parameters.name: HideWeekends
parameters.description: Hides the Saturday and Sunday columns (ReUI parity — its event calendar exposes a weekend-hiding toggle). Default false: with it off the grid renders its exact previous seven-column markup. The 42-cell model is untouched; only rendering and keyboard navigation skip the hidden columns. That matters because arrow navigation moves by raw cell index (+/-1, +/-7) — walking that index across a hidden column would put focus on a cell that is not in the DOM, so navigation runs over the VISIBLE cells instead (see VisibleCellIndices).

parameters.name: MaxVisibleLanes
parameters.description: Max visible pill lanes per day before "+N more". Default DefaultMaxVisibleLanes.

parameters.description: The bookable resources, one column each, in the given order. parameters.name: AnchorDate
parameters.description: Anchor date. Week mode (Days == 7) resolves the containing week via FirstDayOfWeek; Day mode (Days == 1) shows this date only.

parameters.name: Days
parameters.description: Number of day columns: 7 = Week, 1 = Day (spec §1.1). Any other value renders that many columns starting at AnchorDate (wave-3 N-day groundwork, not yet a public view).

parameters.name: SlotMinTime
parameters.description: Earliest visible slot. Default 00:00. Never changes the underlying wall-clock grid math (spec §2.3) — purely a visible-range clamp.

parameters.name: SlotMaxTime
parameters.description: Latest visible slot. Default 24:00.

parameters.name: SlotDuration
parameters.description: How long one grid row represents. Default (null) is one hour, which is the grid this view has always drawn. Rows have to tile an hour exactly or the labels in the gutter drift away from the lines they name, so a value that does not divide 60 is rounded UP to the next one that does (25 minutes becomes 30). Values are clamped to 1..60 minutes.

parameters.name: SnapDuration
parameters.description: How far a drag, resize or drag-create snaps. Defaults to SlotDuration when that is set — dragging onto a line the grid does not draw is the kind of mismatch users read as a bug — and to 15 minutes otherwise, which is what this view snapped to before the grid was configurable.

parameters.name: NowTimeZoneId
parameters.description: IANA zone the NOW-INDICATOR is read in. The grid itself stays wall-clock — the wrapper has already projected the events it hands down (see SchedulerTimeZoneProjection) — but the now line is computed in the browser from the real clock, so without this it would sit at the viewer's local time on a grid drawn for somewhere else.

parameters.name: AlignToWeek
parameters.description: Whether a 7-day grid snaps to the configured week start. True (the default) is the Week view. False makes seven days mean "seven days from the anchor" — the rolling N-day window, which happens to collide with the Week view at exactly this one width.

parameters.name: Editable
parameters.description: Allows events to be dragged (move) and edge-resized. Default true.

parameters.name: Selectable
parameters.description: Allows drag-to-create on empty grid background. Default true.

parameters.name: NowIndicator
parameters.description: Shows the browser-local current-time indicator line (spec §2.2 — positioned and refreshed entirely client-side, never a server-computed value). Default true.

parameters.name: CanDrop
parameters.description: Fail-closed validation predicate for a move/resize drop (spec §3.2), widened to a three-way reject/accept/accept-with-adjustment contract (mirrors ReUI's onEventUpdate) — see SchedulerDropResult. null (default) means no consumer opted in — JS is told via hasCanDrop: false so zero ValidateDrop interop calls happen per drag, not "always permit".

Default false (opt-in, matches the wrapper's own default). Grid interval and snap duration remain out of scope for this pass (still hardcoded — see the report).
